subject: CloudScale invoice shift to AWS Marketplace — migration plan and timeline
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@cloudscale.com>, procurement@cloudscale.com
Cc: 
Date: 2027-05-21T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: CloudScale — option to move renewal invoicing to AWS Marketplace

Hi Emily / CloudScale procurement team,

Thanks again for the productive QBR last week. We heard that your renewal for the Redwood Inference subscription is coming up on June 30 and wanted to propose moving invoicing onto the AWS Marketplace for the renewal period. A Marketplace-based billing flow would let CloudScale: 

- Receive consolidated cloud billing (single line-item)
- Use existing internal procure/payment flows tied to AWS Marketplace purchases
- Simplify future renewals and allow for marketplace credits/promotions (if desired)

High-level ask from us: would CloudScale be open to switching the renewal from direct invoicing to AWS Marketplace billing? If yes, we can share a concise migration checklist (contract amendment + DocuSign flow + sample invoice) and a recommended timeline so this is seamless for your procurement and accounting teams.

Can we schedule a 30-min call this week to walk through the operational steps? If it helps, I can include our marketplace enablement lead and the partner ops contact.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0147
From: Emily Park <emily.park@cloudscale.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CloudScale — option to move renewal invoicing to AWS Marketplace

Hi Diego,

Appreciate the heads-up. Procurement is definitely open to marketplace billing in general, but before we run this up the chain we need a few clarifications:

1) Who is the seller of record (Redwood vs. AWS)?
2) Will pricing/discounts be identical on the marketplace vs our current committed contract?
3) How do we handle unused pre-paid credits or existing proration on the June 30 renewal?
4) Can you provide a sample marketplace invoice and the DocuSign amendment language we would sign?

If you can send the checklist and sample invoice, that would speed our internal review. We can also do a quick call Thursday afternoon.

Thanks —
Emily Park
Head of Procurement, CloudScale Inc
emily.park@cloudscale.com
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: CloudScale marketplace questions — quick plan?

Team,

FYI — CloudScale is open but needs a short packet to send to their finance/GC. Key asks from Emily are: seller-of-record, pricing parity, handling of unused pre-paid credit/proration, and sample invoice/DocuSign language.

Suggested playbook (draft):
- Seller-of-record options: (A) Redwood as SOR (Redwood invoices via AWS MP seller program) or (B) AWS as SOR with Redwood as publisher-managed listing. Recommend option A to preserve existing contractual terms.
- Pricing/discount parity: confirm marketplace SKU will mirror their committed effective price for the renewal term (no surprise uplift). Include mapping table in spreadsheet.
- Credits/proration: propose a one-time credit or pro-rata refund for any pre-paid months overlapping the switch; include sample calculation.
- DocuSign amendment: short amendment accepting marketplace billing + SOW attachment; we provide DocuSign link.
- Timeline: enablement doc + DocuSign within 5 business days; marketplace listing activation 2–3 business days after signature; first marketplace invoice on next monthly bill cycle, effective for June 30 renewal.

Marissa: can you draft a 1-page checklist + sample invoice? Rafael: can you confirm SOR recommendation and whether our partner ops needs to create a publisher-managed listing? Neha: any constraints from finance for credits/proration wording?

I want to keep the external thread short and give them clear next steps.

Thanks,
Diego

-----Original message forwarded-----
On Fri, May 21, 2027 at 11:02 AM Emily Park <emily.park@cloudscale.com> wrote:
> Hi Diego,
> 
> Appreciate the heads-up. Procurement is definitely open to marketplace billing in general, but before we run this up the chain we need a few clarifications:...
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@cloudscale.com>, procurement@cloudscale.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: CloudScale Marketplace migration checklist + sample invoice (attachments)

Hi Emily,

Thanks for the quick reply. Per your questions, attached are: (1) cloudscale-marketplace-checklist.pdf (one-pager with steps and timeline), and (2) aws-billing-sample-invoice.pdf (example marketplace invoice line items and account mapping). I also attached a short migration MOP (migration-mop-up.xlsx) that shows the calculation for proration/credits. Key points below:

- Seller of Record: Redwood as Seller of Record (recommended). This preserves your current commercial terms and allows us to issue marketplace invoices that match the committed effective price.
- Pricing parity: marketplace SKU will be configured to match your existing effective monthly rate for the renewal term; there will be no uplift.
- Credits/proration: if you have any pre-paid or unused term portion overlapping June 30, we will issue a one-time credit equating to the net unused value (calculation in the attached sheet).
- DocuSign: we prepared a single-line amendment accepting marketplace billing + a signature block; we will send a DocuSign link once you confirm.
- Timeline: we recommend signing the amendment by 6/2 to allow listing activation and to have marketplace billing show on the first invoice post-renewal.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review attachments with your finance/GC team this week.
2) Confirm acceptance of Redwood as SOR and parity pricing.
3) We send DocuSign amendment and enable listing upon signature.

If you'd like, we can set a 30-min call Thursday 5/27 to walk your team through the sample invoice and the proration calc.

Attachments: cloudscale-marketplace-checklist.pdf, aws-billing-sample-invoice.pdf, migration-mop-up.xlsx

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Emily Park <emily.park@cloudscale.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudscale.com
Date: 2027-05-30T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CloudScale Marketplace migration checklist + sample invoice (attachments)

Diego —

Thanks for the materials and clear timeline. Procurement reviewed the checklist and the proration calc looks good. We are willing to proceed with Redwood as Seller of Record and accept parity pricing for the renewal term. A few small asks before we sign:

- Can you confirm whether our AWS account ID needs to be linked to the marketplace purchase (yes/no)?
- Please include a one-line credit for unused prepaid months in the amendment (we saw the calc but want the language).
- Send the DocuSign link and the final amendment PDF.

Once we have the DocuSign link procurement will get signatures — target sign-off by 6/2. Appreciate you looping the marketplace ops folks.

Best,
Emily Park
Head of Procurement, CloudScale Inc
